question.prompt: In the expansion of \[ \begin{aligned} &\left(1 + x + x^2 + \cdots + x^{27}\right) \\ &\quad {}\cdot \left(1 + x + x^2 + \cdots + x^{14}\right)^2, \end{aligned} \] what is the coefficient of \(x^{28}?\)

solutions.explanation:
In a polynomial product, each contribution to \(x^{28}\) comes from choosing one term from each factor whose exponents sum to \(28\). All the chosen terms have coefficient \(1\), so the desired coefficient counts these choices.

Treat the two copies of \(1+x+\cdots+x^{14}\) as separate factors. Choose exponents \(b\) and \(c\) from them, with \(0\le b,c\le14\). There are \(15\cdot15=225\) ordered pairs. Each pair forces the exponent from the first factor to be
\[
a=28-b-c.
\]
Because \(b+c\le28\), we always have \(a\ge0\). The other requirement, \(a\le27\), is equivalent to \(b+c\ge1\). Exactly one pair fails this condition: \((b,c)=(0,0)\), which would require the unavailable term \(x^{28}\) from the first factor.

Every remaining pair determines exactly one valid exponent triple, and every contribution to \(x^{28}\) arises this way. Thus the coefficient is
\[
225-1=\boxed{224},
\]
choice C.
solutions.title: Choose exponents from the two shorter factors
